phase3_findings.description: The already-masked guarantee for frames reaching RunSqlTool rests only on build_agent's runner wiring; no type or check enforces it.
MASKED_COLUMNS_ATTR holds one entry per masked position, so duplicate labels repeat in the note; no test pins the attribute for duplicates.
SecretColumnMatcher repeats ResultMaskingConfig's no-words check and self._entries lacks a type annotation.
test_env_wrong_type_fails_naming_setting tests a no-words entry, not a wrong type; no env test covers a wrong-type JSON value or an unknown key.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (four Suggestion findings, no blocking finding)
The PR is ready to merge: all 34 checklist items passed, every acceptance criterion was itemized, and no reviewer raised a finding at or above the Critical threshold.
Rule applied: rule 6 — only findings below the threshold remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)

<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. In `src/sqllens/safety/masking.py` lines 170–188, the guarantee that a frame reaching `RunSqlTool` is already masked rests only on how `build_agent` wraps the runner. No type or check in `RunSqlTool` enforces it, so a `RunSqlTool` built over an unwrapped runner would write secret values without any signal. Today `build_agent` is the only construction path, so behavior is correct. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. In `src/sqllens/safety/masking.py` line 166, the masked-label list holds one entry per masked column position, not one per distinct label. Two columns both labelled `token` give a note reading `token, token`. No test pins the attribute for duplicate labels. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. In `src/sqllens/safety/masking.py` lines 135–140, `SecretColumnMatcher.__init__` repeats the "every entry has words" check that `ResultMaskingConfig` already performs, and `self._entries` has no type annotation. Behavior is correct, because the config check runs first. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. In `tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py` lines 356–361, `test_env_wrong_type_fails_naming_setting` sets an entry with no words, not a value of the wrong type. No test checks a wrong-type JSON environment value or an unknown key supplied through the environment. The TOML versions of both cases are tested and share the same model. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>
